overview.description: Gaps is a single-player patience game in which four rows are arranged in suit sequence from 2 through King. Four gaps are created by removing the aces, and cards can move only into legal next-rank same-suit gaps.

history.origins: Gaps belongs to the Montana family of patience games and appears in 20th-century rule collections under names including Montana and Spaces.
timeline: Early and mid 20th century: Published as part of the Montana family of patience games.
Late 20th century onward: Became common in computer solitaire suites under names such as Gaps and Addiction.
history.evolution: The core mechanism is stable: remove aces, fill gaps by suit and ascending rank, then redeal unsorted cards when blocked. The main variation is redeal count and whether cards are shuffled.
history.cultural: Gaps is widely played as a quick logic-focused solitaire with visible state and low-overhead turns.

setup.players: One player. Gaps is a patience (solitaire) game; a single player plays alone and makes all decisions about which cards to move into gaps and when to redeal.
setup.equipment: One shuffled deck and table space for four rows of thirteen cards.
setup.dealing: Deal all 52 cards face up into four rows of thirteen. Remove all four aces, leaving four empty spaces.

rules.objective: Finish with each row in same-suit order from 2 through King, leaving the four gaps immediately to the right of the Kings.
rules.gameplay: A gap may be filled only by the card that is one rank higher and the same suit as the card immediately to its left. A gap at the far left of a row can be filled only by a 2. Gaps immediately right of a King are dead until redeal. When no legal move exists, gather all cards that are not part of correct left-to-right suit runs, redeal them into the open spaces, and continue. Standard Gaps allows two redeals, for up to three passes total.
keyRules: Only legal successor cards can enter a gap: same suit and exactly one rank higher than the card on the left.
A left-edge gap accepts only a 2.
A gap to the right of a King is dead for that pass.
After all redeals are used, if any row is incomplete, the game is lost.

strategy.basic: Prioritize moves that extend correct suit runs from a 2 because locked runs survive into redeals.
strategy.intermediate: Delay moves that strand Kings in central positions; dead King-right gaps reduce mobility until the next redeal.
strategy.advanced: Before redeal, maximize preserved ordered prefixes in each row so fewer cards re-enter random distribution.
tips: Treat each row as an independent suit runway and protect long correct prefixes.
If several moves are legal, prefer the one that unlocks a second immediate legal successor.

list.name: Addiction
list.description: Same core play but typically allows three redeals rather than two.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Redeal count can be expressed via engine.constants or roundConfig when implementing.

list.name: No-shuffle Redeal
list.description: Unsorted cards are redealt without shuffling, reducing randomness and changing solvability.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Shuffle-on-redeal flag would go in engine or patienceConfig when implemented.

list.name: Unlimited Redeals
list.description: Redeals continue until solved; turns game into a deterministic endurance variant.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Redeal limit override can be added to roundConfig or constants when implementing.

difficulty.easy: Chooses the first legal gap fill and redeals immediately when stuck.
difficulty.medium: Prefers moves that lengthen left-to-right suit runs and reduce dead King-right gaps.
difficulty.hard: Evaluates move trees before redeal to maximize preserved ordered sequences and expected solvability after redeal.

considerations: AI must detect legal successor mapping for each gap in constant time.
Redeal decision quality drives win rate more than single greedy move quality.

phases.label: Initial Layout
phases.notes: Deal four rows of thirteen and remove aces to create four gaps.

phases.label: Gap Fill and Redeal
phases.notes: Fill legal gaps by successor rule. If stuck and redeals remain, redeal unsorted cards into open spaces.

ante.reason: Gaps is solitaire and has no ante or betting phase.

deal.description: Deal the initial layout or execute a redeal of unsorted cards into open spaces.
deal.constraints: Initial deal occurs once; redeal allowed only when no legal gap fill exists and redeals remain.

reveal_market.reason: No market exists in Gaps; all cards are in tableau and stock handling only.

buy_market.reason: Gaps has no purchasing mechanic or market row.

buy_stock.reason: Stock cards are redealt by rule, not bought.

fold.reason: Single-player patience has no fold action.

check.reason: Gaps has no betting rounds and therefore no check action.

call.reason: Gaps has no betting rounds and therefore no call action.

bet.reason: No wagering mechanics are part of standard Gaps rules.

raise.reason: No wagering mechanics are part of standard Gaps rules.

declare.reason: There is no declaration phase in this patience game.

reveal_hand.reason: All cards are face up on tableau, so hand reveal does not apply.

award_pot.reason: Gaps has a binary win or loss outcome and no pot.

play_card.description: Move a card into a gap when it is the same suit and exactly one rank above the card to the left.
play_card.constraints: Left-edge gap only accepts a 2; gaps right of Kings are dead for the current pass.

draw.reason: No draw-to-hand action exists; all cards remain in tableau flow.

discard.description: Remove aces from play after the initial deal to create starting gaps.
discard.constraints: Only aces are discarded and only during setup.

pass.reason: Turns are not passed; the player either fills a gap or redeals when blocked.

bid.reason: No bidding mechanism exists in Gaps.

meld.reason: Gaps is not a meld-making game; cards are sequenced directly on tableau rows.

go_out.reason: Game ends on solved layout or no redeals left, not by a go-out action.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: No hand drawing exists; cards are managed directly in tableau rows.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Only aces are removed during setup, not turn-by-turn discard play.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Standard deck has no wild or action cards in Gaps.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Win condition is ordered tableau completion, not hand shedding.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Gaps is not a capture or fishing game.

edgeCases.text: A gap immediately to the right of a King cannot be filled until the next redeal.
A gap in column one of any row can only be filled by a 2.
On redeal, correctly ordered suit runs from the left edge remain in place while only unsorted cards are collected and redealt.

customLogicNeeded: Successor lookup by suit and rank for each gap.
Detect and preserve maximal left-anchored in-order suit prefixes before redeal.
Apply redeal limit and terminate on unsolved state when limit reached.

engine.deckDescription: The deck is a standard fifty-two-card French-suited pack; all fifty-two cards are dealt face up into four rows of thirteen, then the four aces are removed to create four gaps for this patience game.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits are Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, and Spades; each suit has thirteen cards and gaps are filled only by the correct next rank in the same suit from 2 through King.
engine.rankDescription: Ranks are Ace through King in each suit; aces are removed at setup and the playable sequence in each row is 2 through King in same-suit order, with only the legal successor card filling each gap.
engine.dealPattern: Deal full grid of four rows by thirteen, then remove all aces to form initial gaps.

hero.title: GAPS
hero.subtitle: Montana Solitaire
hero.tagline: Fill each gap with the exact next card and manage redeals.

synthesis.shortDescription: Single-player sequence puzzle where four suit rows must be ordered from 2 to King using strict gap-fill rules.

prompts.human: I need to place only the exact same-suit successor into each gap, and save redeals for stronger preserved runs.
prompts.ai: Game: Gaps. Fill gaps with same-suit next-rank cards, 2 only on left edge, king-right gaps are dead, and only two redeals are allowed in standard play.

scoring.description: Gaps is normally scored as solved or unsolved; some software also reports cards correctly ordered.
scoring.winCondition: All four rows are complete suit sequences from 2 through King with final gaps to the right of each King.

nullReasons.targetScore: Standard Gaps is a binary completion puzzle rather than a fixed-point race.
nullReasons.cardValues: Gaps is scored as solved or unsolved; no per-card point values are used.
